explanation.heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
explanation.text: Compute and interpret sample statistics: mean, median, mode, range, sample proportion, and weighted combined mean. Use sample results to estimate a population quantity while recognizing sampling uncertainty.

explanation.heading: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
explanation.text: A sample is a subset of a population. A sample statistic summarizes observed sample data; a population parameter describes the whole population. A statistic may vary across random samples.

explanation.heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
explanation.text: Sample size n: number observed. Sample mean: sum of values divided by n. Median: middle ordered value. Mode: most frequent value. Range: maximum minus minimum. Sample proportion: successes divided by n.

explanation.heading: CORE RULE
explanation.text: Mean = sum/n; proportion = favorable/n; range = max−min. For groups of sizes n₁ and n₂, combined mean = (n₁×mean₁+n₂×mean₂)/(n₁+n₂). Estimate count = sample proportion × population size.

explanation.heading: HOW IT WORKS
explanation.text: 1. Identify the requested statistic and sample size. 2. Sort data for median, count frequencies for mode, or sum for mean. 3. For proportions, use sample successes over sample size. 4. Weight group means by group sizes. 5. Keep conclusions appropriately approximate.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — MEAN
explanation.text: Sample values 4, 6, 8, 10. Mean=(4+6+8+10)/4=7. The mean balances the total across observations.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — MEDIAN
explanation.text: Sorted sample 2, 4, 7, 9, 12 has median 7. For 2, 4, 7, 9, the median is (4+7)/2=5.5.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — PROPORTION
explanation.text: In a random sample of 80, 28 prefer cycling. Sample proportion=28/80=0.35, or 35%. This estimates the population preference, not an exact census count.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — WEIGHTED MEAN
explanation.text: Eight students average 72; twelve average 82. Combined mean=(8×72+12×82)/20=78. Averaging 72 and 82 equally would ignore group sizes.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — ESTIMATING A COUNT
explanation.text: If 30 of 120 surveyed residents support a proposal, estimated proportion=1/4. In a population of 500, estimated supporters≈500/4=125, subject to sampling uncertainty.

explanation.heading: SAMPLE TABLE / VISUAL STRATEGY
explanation.text: Organize observations in a sorted table and count each value's frequency. For two groups, show columns for sample size, group mean, and group total n×mean. These deterministic arithmetic tables prevent unweighted-average errors.

explanation.heading: COMMON MISTAKES
explanation.text: Do not confuse a sample statistic with a known population parameter. Sort before finding the median. Do not divide by population size when calculating a sample proportion. Do not average group means without weighting by sample size.

explanation.heading: EXAM STRATEGY
explanation.text: Check whether the question asks for a statistic, an estimate, or a population parameter. Use totals to combine means. For even-sized samples, average the two middle values. Round only when requested.

explanation.heading: QUICK CHECK
explanation.text: Sample 2,4,6 has mean 4. Sample 1,3,7,9 has median 5. If 15 of 60 respondents agree, sample proportion is 1/4. Equal-size group means 10 and 20 combine to 15.

explanation.heading: LESSON RECAP
explanation.text: Mean=sum/n; median=middle ordered value; range=max−min; proportion=count/n; combined mean is size-weighted. Sample-based population estimates are approximate.

explanation.heading: NEXT STEP
explanation.text: Solve 18 practice questions, check 18 worked solutions, then take the five-question test. Review the bilingual full-lesson instructional routes.

practice.question: What is the sample mean of 2, 4, 6, and 8?
What is the median of the ordered sample 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
practice.solution: The middle of five ordered values is the third, 7.

practice.question: In a sample of 50, 12 prefer tea. What is the sample proportion?
What is the mode of the sample 4, 7, 7, 9, 13?
practice.solution: Seven occurs twice; every other value once.

practice.question: Among 80 surveyed students, 28 prefer cycling. What proportion prefer cycling?
Find the median of the ordered sample 2, 3, 7, 10, 11, 17.
Twelve sampled test scores sum to 960. What is the sample mean?
Six observations have mean 18. Five sum to 85. What is the sixth observation?
What is the median of the ordered sample 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16?
practice.solution: Seven observations: the fourth value is 9.

practice.question: 30 of 120 randomly sampled residents support a plan. Estimate how many of 500 residents support it.
45 of 150 sampled voters support a candidate. Estimate supporters among 900 voters.
Two samples of ten observations each have means 15 and 18. What is their combined mean?
Six observations 8, 9, 10, 10, 11, 12 have mean 10. Add 16. What is the new mean?
practice.solution: Original sum=60. New total=76 over seven observations.

practice.question: A sample of 200 contains 95 supporters. What is the sample proportion?
Sample A has 12 supporters among 30; sample B has 42 among 70. Pool the samples. What is the overall support proportion?
Three samples: n=20 mean=12, n=30 mean=15, n=50 mean=18. Find the combined mean.

test.question: Nine of 36 surveyed people prefer buses. What is the sample proportion?
Find the median of the ordered sample 1, 4, 6, 9.
40 of 160 sampled residents support a plan. Estimate supporters among 900 residents.
A sample of 15 students has mean 70; another of 25 has mean 86. What is their combined mean?

english.title: Lesson objective
english.narration: Learn to calculate and interpret statistics from sample data.

english.title: Population and sample
english.narration: A sample is part of a larger population.

english.title: Sample statistic
english.narration: A statistic describes a sample; a parameter describes a population.

english.title: Mean
english.narration: Add observed values and divide by sample size.

english.title: Median
english.narration: Sort observations; average two middle values when the sample size is even.

english.title: Mode and range
english.narration: The mode occurs most often; range is maximum minus minimum.

english.title: Sample proportion
english.narration: Divide successes by the sample size.

english.title: Estimation
english.narration: Multiply sample proportion by population size for an estimate.

english.title: Combined mean
english.narration: Combine group totals and divide by combined sample size.

english.title: Why weights matter
english.narration: Do not average group means equally when group sizes differ.

english.title: Sampling uncertainty
english.narration: Different random samples may produce different estimates.

english.title: Exam recap
english.narration: Identify the statistic, compute carefully, and interpret the estimate.

arabic.title: المجتمع والعينة
arabic.narration: العينة جزء من المجتمع الإحصائي الأكبر.

arabic.title: إحصاء العينة
arabic.narration: إحصاء العينة يصف العينة، والمعلمة تصف المجتمع كله.

arabic.title: المتوسط
arabic.narration: اجمع القيم واقسم على عدد المشاهدات.

arabic.title: الوسيط
arabic.narration: رتب القيم وخذ الوسط أو متوسط القيمتين الوسطيتين.

arabic.title: المنوال والمدى
arabic.narration: المنوال الأكثر تكراراً والمدى أكبر قيمة ناقص أصغر قيمة.

arabic.title: نسبة العينة
arabic.narration: اقسم عدد الحالات المناسبة على حجم العينة.

arabic.title: التقدير
arabic.narration: اضرب نسبة العينة في حجم المجتمع للحصول على تقدير.

arabic.title: المتوسط الموزون
arabic.narration: اجمع إجماليات المجموعات ثم اقسم على مجموع الأحجام.

arabic.title: أهمية الأوزان
arabic.narration: لا تأخذ متوسطاً بسيطاً لمتوسطات مجموعات مختلفة الحجم.

arabic.title: عدم اليقين
arabic.narration: تختلف تقديرات العينات العشوائية بسبب تباين العينات.

arabic.title: مراجعة الامتحان
arabic.narration: حدد المطلوب واحسب بدقة وفسّر النتيجة.
